title: Revisit 3 news exam: pre-registration (sealed before any model call on these items)
decision_under_test: For a newly tracked CVE in a Debian 12 bookworm source package, decide URGENT (the LTS team ships a DLA) vs NEXT / WONTFIX / NOTAFF.
answers: Debian's own records only: the bookworm decision in the Debian security tracker and the DSA/DLA lists fetched 2026-10-26 16:09 +08:00, labelled with the unchanged gold rule of ../revisit/prep_data.py gold_label (URGENT = a DSA/DLA lists the bookworm package for the CVE). No human or AI labels.

selection.news_set: A: every CVE named in a Debian DSA or DLA dated 2026-10-01 .. 2026-10-26. B: every CVE CISA KEV added with dateAdded in 2026-10 (catalog 2026.10.23). Item = (CVE, source package) for every source package the tracker lists, kept when Debian has a bookworm decision. Excluded packages (bulk whole-version updates, same as every earlier exam): linux, linux-* backport kernels, chromium, firefox-esr, thunderbird, webkit2gtk, wpewebkit.
selection.mix_set: Same size as the news set. Pool: (CVE, pkg) whose CVE first appears after the 2026-09-01 snapshot, not in A or B, package not excluded, bookworm record <no-dsa>, <postponed> or <not-affected> (or no bookworm line and unstable <not-affected>), gold NEXT or NOTAFF. For each news item in (cve, pkg) order, one pool item of the same package type (Section of the bookworm Sources entry) is drawn with random.Random(20261026); if that type is used up, from the whole remaining pool. Each news item and its drawn mix item form a pair.
selection.not_hand_picked: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, php8.2) is in the news set only because DLA-4848-1 / DSA-6574-1 (2026-10-21) match rule A.
selection.time_wall: Each item sees tracker history only up to the monthly snapshot before the CVE first appears. CVEs already in the earliest snapshot (2026-06-01): wall 2026-06-01 and every record of that same CVE removed from what S, OURS, NN and R1 see.

arms.S: evidence path, strong baseline without Meterless: same Nemotron request via Nightshift; policy + item facts + the package's 20 most recent raw tracker decision lines before the wall (core/triage_agent.py run_S).
arms.OURS: memory path, always trust memory: Planner reads H-MEM (current stances after supersession, relevance recall, stance changes) -> Executor -> Evaluator (core/triage_agent.py run_OURS).
arms.GATED: the frozen gatekeeper core/gate.py (byte-identical to ../revisit2/gate.py, frozen 2026-10-23 before fresh300) chooses the OURS or the S answer per item from the two answers and H-MEM features (data/news_feat.json, computed before any model call). The product runs the same rules as the Guard stage of its Meterless Scout Intent implementation; a test must show Scout and gate.py give identical choices on every scored item.
arms.NN: time-walled TF-IDF nearest past decision inside the package; no model.
arms.R1: rule: repeat the package's most recent recorded bookworm decision before the wall (NEXT if none); no model.
arms.reported_only: package-mode baseline; ablation "gatekeeper without the H-MEM rule" (rules agree + class_unreliable only); removing the Scout gatekeeper = OURS or S alone.
arms.code_changes_vs_earlier_runs: core/triage_agent.py = ../revisit/triage_agent.py with data paths switched to the news exam and the own-CVE history filter (lines marked REVISIT3). Prompts and Planner/Executor/Evaluator logic unchanged.

run_rules.nightshift: every model call through Meterless Nightshift only; meterless-scope iso-<uuid4> per request (REVISIT_SCOPE=iso); stream, tier-split off; one request in flight in total (the box is shared with two other projects); backoff 15/30/60/120/180 s, 8 tries.
run_rules.model: nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b requested; Nightshift routes inside its Nemotron lanes; served model logged per call.
run_rules.order: pairs in the order random.Random(20261027).shuffle(sorted pair keys); news item then mix item; S then OURS. New pairs are not started after 2026-10-27 05:30 +08:00. Because the order is a sealed random permutation, the completed pairs are a random subset of the exam.
run_rules.scored_set: every pair whose two items both have S and OURS answers. Unparsed replies count as the parser default (NEXT), as in every earlier run.

metric.main: URGENT F1 (and URGENT recall) over the scored items
metric.secondary: macro-F1 over the four classes; per-class table; news half only
metric.bootstrap: paired bootstrap over items, 2,000 resamples, random.Random(11), 95% interval = sorted[50], sorted[1949]; package-cluster bootstrap reported, not deciding.

gate.rule: PASS iff at least 50 complete pairs AND the lower 95% bound of GATED - S URGENT F1 > 0.
gate.no_changes: The rule, the metric, the arms, the scored set and the code hashes below are not changed after this file is sealed.
gate.if_fail: The product is still finished and submitted (user decision 2026-10-26). README then states the failed gate with its numbers and narrows the claim to what passed (e.g. the reopen watcher and the measured trade-off), without claiming the memory gatekeeper improves urgent detection.
